title: Accelerated SDK Signal & Quickstart Pipeline
creator: Maya Chen
description: Summary: Create an accelerated, instrumentation-first pipeline to drive measurable adoption of SDKs, docs, and quickstarts. Problem: current onboarding signal is fragmented (docs views, SDK downloads, console signups) and latency between changes and observable impact is 4+ weeks. Objective: deliver a repeatable tracking and rollout workflow that shortens feedback loop to 7 days and lifts activation for new SDK consumers by +25% in Q2. Scope: SDK release artifacts (node/py/go), quickstart templates, docs quickstart pages, example apps, and a lightweight analytics/experiment layer integrated with Console and the Redwood API. Exclusions: billing model changes and dedicated capacity pricing are out of scope for this initiative.
success_metrics: 7-day activation rate measured from first SDK call: target +25% relative improvement
Reduction of time-to-evidence for doc/SDK change to <7 days
Number of unique quickstart runs per week: target +40%
Instrumented funnel coverage >= 90% for top 5 onboarding flows
milestones: 2026-02-05: Kickoff and signal design (definitions for activation, retention)
2026-03-12: Quickstart templates updated and telemetry hooks added

risks: Telemetry variance: sampling differences between hosted and private deployments may bias metrics
SDK maintenance: extra surface area may increase engineering load without commensurate usage
Privacy/regulatory: customers in Private/VPC may not allow telemetry; fallback attribution will be noisy
Dependency on runtime changes (ENG-23789) could block instrumentation hooks
rollout_plan: Phase 1: opt-in telemetry via SDK flags + Console toggle for early access teams. Phase 2: default enablement for new signups and first-run quickstarts with clear consent flows. Use canary cohorts (10%->50%->100%) with safety gates tied to error rates and retention signals. Employ experiment-compare to baseline for activation metric.
telemetry_plan: Use lightweight event schema (SDK_CALL, QUICKSTART_RUN, DOC_VIEW, EXAMPLE_EXECUTE) tagged with anonymous cohort_id and optional customer_id where consented. Events flow to internal analytics pipeline and a near-real-time dashboard (latency SLA: <5m). For Private deployments, provide a local emitter and a periodic signed-summary ping to avoid raw telemetry export.
stakeholders: Customer Success: Rajiv Menon (outreach for early access)
notes: We will reuse the SDK metrics schema defined in ENG-1842 to keep event footprint small.
Design needs a clear first-run checklist for quickstarts to avoid support spikes.
Plan to include a 'run with sandbox API key' option in quickstarts to improve conversion from docs.
Consider an initial hack-week to build example-app variants for top integrators.
